entities.summary:
Adergoudounbades was a prominent Sasanian nobleman, general, and kanarang during the reigns of Kavadh I and Khosrow I. His life is known only through the work of the Byzantine historian Procopius. Born into a powerful Persian family, Adergoudounbadēs was likely the son of Shapur IV or another high-ranking noble. He rose to prominence during the Sasanian Empire's expansion into Anatolia and the Caucasus.

Adergoudounbades played a key role in several military campaigns against the Roman Empire, including the Battle of Callinicum and the Siege of Amida. His success on the battlefield earned him great wealth and influence within the empire. However, his later years were marked by controversy and turmoil, as he became embroiled in power struggles with other nobles.

The legacy of Adergoudounbades can be seen in the many Sasanian military tactics and strategies that were adopted by subsequent empires. His life serves as a testament to the enduring impact of the Sasanian Empire on the ancient world.

Adergoudounbades' native name was probably Adurgundbad, an abbreviation of Adurgushnaspbad. The Byzantine historian Procopius referred to him as Adergoudounbades in his History of the Wars.

One of the most striking aspects of Adergoudounbades' life is the limited information available about his personal life and relationships. Despite his prominent position within the Sasanian Empire, very little is known about his family or early life.
